Build a brms formula in the congruence–bias parameterisation

Source: R/bf_mfd.R
bf_mfd.Rd

Builds the brms non-linear formula for the congruence–bias parameterisation, in which the native parameters of a bipois() or binegbin() model are functions of the congruence–bias coordinates: the midpoint M of the two expected counts, the congruence f, the source bias (through delta, its inverse hyperbolic tangent), and, for binegbin, the overdispersions kappa. Each coordinate then takes its own linear predictor. A predictor such as site in the formula for logM alone multiplies all three rates by a common factor, so the congruence and the source bias are the same at every site. In the native parameterisation, the same model needs the predictor in all three rates, with the coefficients constrained to be equal.

Usage

bf_mfd(formula, ...)

Arguments

formula

The response part of the model, written without ~: y1 | vint(y2) for bipois() and binegbin(), and y1 | vint(y2, y1_obs) for bipois_partialobs() and binegbin_partialobs(). The response is passed to the brms formula unchanged.

...

Two-sided formulae, one for each coordinate, in any order. The left-hand side names the coordinate and the right-hand side gives its linear predictor, as in logM ~ 0 + site or delta ~ 1. Every coordinate of the chosen set is required, including those with an intercept only.

Value

A brmsformula object, as returned by brms::bf().

Details

The coordinates are related to the native parameters by

$$\mu = M f, \quad \lambda_1 = M (1 - f)(1 + \beta), \quad \lambda_2 = M (1 - f)(1 - \beta), \quad \beta = \tanh \delta,$$

where \(\mu\) is mu, the rate of the shared component, and \(\lambda_1\) and \(\lambda_2\) are lambdaone and lambdatwo, the rates of the source-exclusive components. Each NB2 (inverse) dispersion parameter \(\phi\) is \(1/\kappa^2\), where \(\kappa\) is the corresponding overdispersion. The non-linear parameters are logM (\(\log M\)), logitf (\(\operatorname{logit} f\)), delta (\(\delta\)), and the overdispersions. logM, logitf, and delta are unbounded, so their linear predictors need no link. The overdispersions must be positive (see Priors). mfd_to_dpars() computes the native parameters from the same identities.

Sets of coordinates. The set of coordinate formulae supplied determines the dispersion structure. logM, logitf, and delta are always required. The three valid sets are:

  • logM, logitf, delta, kappas, kappaxone, and kappaxtwo: a separate overdispersion for the shared component and for each exclusive component, for binegbin() and binegbin_partialobs().

  • logM, logitf, delta, kappas, and kappax: one overdispersion, kappax, for both exclusive components, so that shapexone equals shapextwo, for binegbin() and binegbin_partialobs().

  • logM, logitf, and delta: no overdispersion, for bipois() and bipois_partialobs().

Any other set stops with an error. The family passed to brms::brm() must match the set: a set with overdispersions written for a bipois model declares dpars that the family does not have.

The generated formula. For the second set with a site effect on logM,

bf_mfd(
  y1 | vint(y2),
  logM   ~ 0 + site,
  logitf ~ 1,
  delta  ~ 1,
  kappas ~ 1,
  kappax ~ 1
)

returns the same formula as

bf(y1 | vint(y2) ~ 1, nl = TRUE) +
  nlf(mu        ~ logM + log_inv_logit(logitf)) +
  nlf(lambdaone ~ log(2) + logM + log1m_inv_logit(logitf) + log_inv_logit(2 * delta)) +
  nlf(lambdatwo ~ log(2) + logM + log1m_inv_logit(logitf) + log_inv_logit(-2 * delta)) +
  nlf(shapes    ~ -2 * log(kappas)) +
  nlf(shapexone ~ -2 * log(kappax)) +
  nlf(shapextwo ~ -2 * log(kappax)) +
  lf(logM ~ 0 + site, logitf ~ 1, delta ~ 1, kappas ~ 1, kappax ~ 1)

The first set replaces the two kappax lines with shapexone ~ -2 * log(kappaxone) and shapextwo ~ -2 * log(kappaxtwo); the third set omits all three dispersion lines.

Priors. Every coordinate is a non-linear parameter, to which brms gives a flat, improper prior unless one is set. We recommend a prior on each, written with class = "b" and nlpar set to the name of the coordinate. The expression \(-2 \log \kappa\) is undefined for \(\kappa \le 0\), so a prior on an overdispersion with an intercept-only formula needs lb = 0, as in prior(normal(0, 1), class = "b", nlpar = "kappas", lb = 0). The worked example in vignette("bicountbrms") gives priors for every coordinate.

bf_mfd() adds no family, Stan function, or post-processing method. The fitted model is a bipois or binegbin fit whose native parameters are non-linear functions of the coordinates, and posterior_epred(), posterior_predict(), and log_lik() dispatch to the family methods as for any other fit.

See also

mfd_to_dpars(), dpars_to_mfd(), bipois(), bipois_partialobs(), binegbin(), binegbin_partialobs()

Examples

# A site effect on the midpoint alone, with one overdispersion for both
# exclusive components
bf_mfd(
  y1 | vint(y2),
  logM   ~ 0 + site,
  logitf ~ 1,
  delta  ~ 1,
  kappas ~ 1,
  kappax ~ 1
)
#> y1 | vint(y2) ~ 1 
#> mu ~ logM + log_inv_logit(logitf)
#> lambdaone ~ log(2) + logM + log1m_inv_logit(logitf) + log_inv_logit(2 * delta)
#> lambdatwo ~ log(2) + logM + log1m_inv_logit(logitf) + log_inv_logit(-2 * delta)
#> shapes ~ -2 * log(kappas)
#> shapexone ~ -2 * log(kappax)
#> shapextwo ~ -2 * log(kappax)
#> logM ~ 0 + site
#> logitf ~ 1
#> delta ~ 1
#> kappas ~ 1
#> kappax ~ 1

# A partially paired design with Poisson components
bf_mfd(
  y1 | vint(y2, y1_obs),
  logM   ~ 0 + site,
  logitf ~ 1,
  delta  ~ 1
)
#> y1 | vint(y2, y1_obs) ~ 1 
#> mu ~ logM + log_inv_logit(logitf)
#> lambdaone ~ log(2) + logM + log1m_inv_logit(logitf) + log_inv_logit(2 * delta)
#> lambdatwo ~ log(2) + logM + log1m_inv_logit(logitf) + log_inv_logit(-2 * delta)
#> logM ~ 0 + site
#> logitf ~ 1
#> delta ~ 1
